title: Machine learning predicts genotype positivity in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
summary: Three machine learning models were built on clinical and cardiac imaging data from 102 Columbia patients and tested on 76 patients from Massachusetts General Hospital; 63 of 178 patients (35%) were genotype positive. The random forest model reached an AUROC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.85-0.99) in the test set, above the Toronto HCM Genotype Score (0.77, 95% CI 0.65-0.90). Cohorts are small and retrospective, so the result is a prediction benchmark, not evidence about screening outcomes.
ai_technology: Random forest and gradient boosted decision tree models on clinical and cardiac imaging data

evidence.tested: Trained on 102 patients and tested on an independent set of 76 patients, compared with the Toronto and Mayo genotype scores.
evidence.unknown: Performance in larger or prospective cohorts and effect on family screening decisions; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts which patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy will test positive for a pathogenic genotype.
